solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Out when one takes in skirt for alteration

indicators.note: altering means changing, so the combined letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dressmaker sets aside a skirt to be taken in while a colleague is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like a word about absence, but here it means striking workers; the tailoring vocabulary hides the container and anagram signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who have walked out in an industrial dispute are said to be on strike.

clue.text: Rotten being on the rocks, getting job

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
a drink on the rocks is served with ice

explanation.surface: A failing business on the rocks, yet someone lands a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' suggests ruin, but means served over ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a post or position of duty, a job.

clue.text: Split second to meet below

parts.note: under is a synonym for below

explanation.surface: A quick arrangement to meet downstairs, then part.
explanation.definitionFit: To sunder is to split apart, an old literary verb.

clue.text: Hardliners, half crazed, revolted

indicators.note: made crazy, so the five letters are scrambled
the back half of the ten-letter word is taken

explanation.surface: Militants, some of them half mad, rose in rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the second five letters of HARDLINERS, INERS, which 'crazed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have risen up have rebelled or revolted against authority.

clue.text: Having made bloomer, perhaps, required to speak out

indicators.note: said out loud, the word for required sounds like the entry

parts.note: needed means required

explanation.surface: Someone who has blundered must own up.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British loaf of bread, so making one involves working the dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough for a bloomer loaf is worked by hand before baking.

clue.text: Jokey word for 'discipline'?

parts.note: a word that is ..., rather like a joke, also means to chastise

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a playful term meaning discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as PUN-ISH the word describes something jokey or punning, and whole it means to discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: To punish is to discipline or chastise, and pun-ish would describe a jokey word.

clue.text: Later streaks in nude, tipsy as always

indicators.note: drunk and unsteady, so all the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunk naked streaker dashes on later, as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'streaks in' is a container signal dressed as a streaker's run onto the pitch; 'tipsy' then shuffles the combined nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unaltered stays exactly the same as it always was.

clue.text: Finally, then, I will readjust, taking aim

indicators.note: the letters of then and I are adjusted into a new order

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Someone resolves at last to rethink and take aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will readjust' rearranges THEN and I to make IN THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, after everything, which is finally.

clue.text: Like a tail-ender, devil take it!

definitions.meaning: placed furthest back, last of all in the line
the proverb says the devil take the one at the back, so this word completes it

explanation.surface: A last-placed cricketer swears as things go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: A tail-ender is a cricket term for a low-order batsman; the proverb is 'every man for himself and the devil take the hindmost'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindmost means furthest behind, the very last, like the back of a queue.

clue.text: Find he is bound over

indicators.note: bound can mean leaping about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A discovery: he is tied up and handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is over it has come to an end, completed.

clue.text: Shut up or having been banished, for having a gun

indicators.note: the letters of the word or are sent away from the word that follows

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun of the Second World War

explanation.surface: Someone is locked away or exiled for carrying a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been banished' removes OR from FOR, leaving F. The Sten gun is a standard crossword weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten a door or window is to shut it up securely.

clue.text: Work up parts so uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up reverses the letters
the word up parts the two letters of so

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Effort put into uplifting sections of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' puts UP between S and O, giving SUPO; 'uplifting' turns it upside down in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work.

clue.text: Expurgated version of 'Hit the Jackpot'

definitions.meaning: with offensive material removed, made decent
won a lot of money, made a big profit

explanation.surface: A bowdlerised edition of a book or song called 'Hit the Jackpot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idiomatic: a text purged of rudeness, and a gambler who scooped a fortune.

clue.text: Covering hot period, it measures heat

indicators.note: the word for period wraps around the letter for hot

parts.note: a term is a period of time, such as a school term
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A device that tracks heat through a hot spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat energy, used in gas billing in Britain.

clue.text: Shouted 'Evacuate out from building!'

indicators.note: evacuating means emptying, so the letters of out are cleared from the first word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warden yelled an order to clear the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evacuate' takes OUT from SHOUTED, leaving four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is a simple building, often used for storage in a garden.

clue.text: In short supply, which is almost beyond comprehension

definitions.meaning: getting something means understanding it, so this is nearly impossible to grasp

explanation.surface: Something scarce that is also nearly impossible to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means scarce, and with get meaning understand it also means difficult to grasp.

clue.text: Jumps when rider turns and gives signal

indicators.note: the letters for the rider are turned round

parts.note: a postscript, PS, is a rider added to a letter
rings means sounds a bell as a signal

explanation.surface: A horseman wheels round and signals to the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rider' looks equestrian but is a postscript, PS; 'turns' flips it to SP.
explanation.definitionFit: Springs and jumps are synonyms as verbs for leaping.

clue.text: Willing, given medicine, to swallow odd sip

indicators.note: the word for given medicine takes the scrambled letters inside it

parts.note: dosed means given a dose of medicine

indicators.note: strange, so the letters of sip are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient, dosed, is willing to swallow an odd sip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' sits at the start as an adjective; the medical scene hides that 'to swallow' is a container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disposed to do something is being inclined or willing to do it.

clue.text: It encourages stubborn mule to go on

definitions.text: It encourages stubborn mule to go on

parts.words: It encourages stubborn mule to go on
parts.note: a mule is also a backless slipper, so this tool eases a tight one onto the foot

explanation.walkthrough: 'mule' suggests the animal but is a type of slipper.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoehorn is a curved tool that helps a foot slide into tight footwear.

clue.text: Succeed in getting their dithering straightened out

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word their, wavering and then sorted, gets its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting indecisive people to sort themselves out successfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' reads as achieving something, but here means taking over from someone, as an heir does.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone, as an heir does, is to take over their position or estate.

clue.text: As far as 'Wrap up garbage'

parts.note: to means as far as, as in up to here
wrap up is slang for be quiet, and sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone tells another to keep quiet about rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Audibly lamented superciliousness

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word for lamented is matched by sound

parts.note: sighed is to have lamented with a long breath

explanation.surface: Someone moaned out loud about another's haughtiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Side is informal British slang for a haughty, superior manner, as in 'putting on side'.

clue.text: One needs an H in 'hairdo'

indicators.note: the letter given goes inside the word meaning one, as the clue says it needs it in

parts.note: single means one
the letter H given directly

explanation.surface: A spelling reminder that 'hairdo' contains an H.
explanation.definitionFit: A shingle is a short, tapered women's haircut popular in the 1920s.

clue.text: He displays erudition — a front when finding way around

indicators.note: the word for way goes around the others

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
the van is the front of an army or procession

explanation.surface: A scholar puts on a show, going round the long way.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person, someone of great erudition.

clue.text: Silly story about egghead and aphrodisiac?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about the head of egg
foolish, so the letters of story are jumbled

parts.note: the head of the word egg is E

explanation.surface: A daft tale about an intellectual and a love potion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives E, the head of EGG.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellfish of this kind are traditionally reputed to arouse desire, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Excuse ('Little time') that's tailor-made

parts.note: a plea is an excuse offered in defence
T is a small abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A tailor's brief apology for being late with the suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold sewn into cloth, the kind of thing a tailor makes.

clue.text: Cuckoo in a cage

parts.note: a bird caged up, or someone driven mad by being locked up in prison, which is stir in slang

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' poses as the bird but means mad; stir is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir-crazy describes someone driven mad by long confinement, as in prison.

clue.text: Finish unfinished cupboard

indicators.note: the word for cupboard loses its last letter

parts.note: a closet is a cupboard

explanation.surface: A carpenter has to complete a half-built cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To close something is to end or finish it, as in closing a meeting.

clue.text: On taking good look round, prepared to absorb

indicators.note: the word for look goes round the other letters

parts.note: to spy is to look

indicators.note: the first word takes on the next letter beside it

explanation.surface: Someone poised to soak up information while having a good look about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spongy is soft and porous, ready to soak up liquid.

clue.text: Crass, ranting ludicrously about nothing

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about the letter for nothing
the word ranting is rearranged absurdly

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A boor rants absurdly about nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ludicrously' rearranges RANTING, and 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass and ignorant both describe someone stupid and lacking understanding.

clue.text: Mean, having got home, to put back key

parts.note: a den is a home or lair

indicators.note: the word to is reversed, placed backwards

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone arrives home and returns a key, as intended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is the note E; 'put back' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote something is to mean or signify it.

clue.text: Outside court, ring newly freed subject of court martial?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the other two pieces
the word freed is made anew, its letters rearranged

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A prisoner is released outside court, a ring of people around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' rearranges FREED to DEFER, which goes outside CT and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier who deserts to the enemy could face trial by a military tribunal.
